name: VIX futures basis carry (short VIX in contango)

origin.source_title: The VIX Futures Basis: Evidence and Trading Strategies (Journal of Derivatives 21(3), 54-69)

how_it_works.simple: VIX futures usually cost more than the VIX itself and drift down towards it as they expire. Sell them when that gap is large, buy them when it is upside down, and hedge with S&P 500 futures.
how_it_works.analogy: Like selling umbrellas at a markup on a cloudy day that usually stays dry.
how_it_works.precise: The daily roll is (front VIX future minus VIX) divided by business days to settlement. Short one front VIX future when the roll is above 0.10 points (contango), long when it is below -0.10 (backwardation), hold five business days, and hedge market exposure with mini S&P 500 futures using out-of-sample hedge ratios.

rule: Each day after 3:00 pm Chicago time: if the front VIX future (the nearest contract with at least 10 business days to settlement) is in contango with a daily roll above 0.10 points, short it and buy mini S&P 500 futures as a hedge; if in backwardation with a daily roll below -0.10, buy it and sell the hedge; exit after 5 business days.
data_needed: Daily VIX futures settlement prices by contract
economic_rationale: Investors pay a premium to hold VIX futures as crash insurance, so the futures sit above the expected future VIX and sellers collect the difference (Simon and Campasano argue the basis is a risk premium, not a forecast).
why_it_might_fail: Short volatility loses suddenly and heavily. On 5 February 2018 the VIX more than doubled in a day and the XIV short-VIX note was terminated after losing almost all its value. The sample (2006 to 2011) is short.

reported_results.source: Simon and Campasano (2012 working paper), EFMA 2013 version
reported_results.market: VIX futures hedged with E-mini S&P 500
reported_results.notes: Mean profits after costs of $539 per contract for short trades and $908 for long trades (5-day holds), with round-trip costs of about $60 a trade including full bid-ask spreads. With equity of 5 times required margin the paper reports about 20% a year compounded; higher leverage gives more, which the authors call an extreme upper bound. Published version (2014) not read; numbers may differ.

post_publication_evidence: Not checked by us yet. The February 2018 VIX spike (the end of XIV) happened after the paper and is the obvious test.

relevance.reason: Short-volatility products and bots were popular with retail traders before 2018, and Verify should be able to show how a steady-looking record can end.

research.notes: Cboe may publish per-contract VIX futures history free, but the path we tried returned 403; not checked further. Added by Amanda's library batch on 2026-10-25 (options, intraday and equity anomalies that retail traders and bots claim to use).
